item.subject: Mathematics
item.stem:
On the map, 1 cm represents 10 km on the land.

[Image: Map showing towns and roads]

On the land, about how far apart are the towns Melville and Folley?
item.figure_description: A rectangular map showing three towns marked with dots: Melville near the top center, Mockem on the middle left, and Folley to the lower right. A thick curved black line representing "Red River" runs diagonally across the map from the lower-left to the upper-right. Thin lines represent roads: one goes vertically down through Melville and Mockem, and another connects Melville curving down and to the right, crossing the Red River and passing through Folley. In the bottom right corner of the map, an inset box contains a scale line segment marked with vertical end-ticks labeled "1 cm = 10 km". On the map, the straight-line distance between Melville and Folley is approximately 5 times the length of the 1 cm scale bar.
item.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.stem:
[Image: Front of a building with a car parked outside]

The car is 3.5 m long. About how long is the building?
reference_items.figure_description: A line drawing showing the front facade of a single-story building. In the center is a double door with an arched window above it. Symmetrically flanking the doors are six identical rectangular windows with multipaned sashes: three windows to the left of the door and three to the right. Parked on the ground along the far left of the building facade is a black car, positioned spanning the space of roughly the first two windows. The length of the entire building is approximately four times the length of the car.

reference_items.stem:
Mike and Katy are planning a day trip for their class.

They plan to go from their school in Ourtown to one of the towns of Acton, Burley, Camford, or Darley.

[Image: Map of Ourtown and surrounding towns]

descriptors: Acton – Yes; Burley – No; Darley - Yes
2 out of 3 correct
Other Incorrect (including crossed out/erased, stray marks, illegible, or off task)
Blank

reference_items.figure_description:
A map enclosed in a wavy rectangular border, labeled "Map drawn to scale" in the bottom-left corner. Five locations are marked with solid black dots and labels:
- "Ourtown" is located in the lower-middle portion of the map.
- "Acton" is northwest of Ourtown, connected to Ourtown by a straight path line.
- "Burley" is directly north of Acton, connected to Acton by a vertical straight path line.
- "Camford" is northeast of Ourtown, connected to Ourtown by a straight path line.
- "Darley" is southeast of Ourtown, connected to Ourtown by a straight path line.
There are three clusters of small stylized pine tree symbols: one cluster between the path to Acton and the path to Camford, one cluster west of Ourtown, and one cluster southeast of Ourtown between the paths to Camford and Darley.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (eighth-grade mathematics).

In the actual triangle ABC, what is the length of side BC?
reference_items.figure_description:
Two right triangles are shown side by side:
- On the left is triangle ABC: vertical leg AB on the left, horizontal base BC on the bottom, with vertex B at the right-angle corner. Hypotenuse AC is labeled "6 cm". Inside angle A is labeled "50°" and inside angle C is labeled "40°".
- On the right is a larger triangle DEF: vertical leg DE on the left, horizontal base EF on the bottom labeled "15 cm", with vertex E at the right-angle corner. Hypotenuse DF is labeled "20 cm". Inside angle D is labeled "50°" and inside angle F is labeled "40°".

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

location.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's location (difficulty) parameter b? b is on a logit scale on which the students of the calibration average about 0; a higher b means a harder item. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

guessing.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's guessing (lower asymptote) parameter c: the probability that a student of very low ability answers it correctly, such as by guessing among the options? Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration.
